actual_scope: For four dirty scalar roles over F2[UT5(Z)], determine whether the target diag([g1*g2],[g2],[g3],[g4]) can be realized in three paid factors when each address letter is one of the eight signed simple roots and each coupling is any binary rank-one idempotent.
scope_change_reason: Fix one torsion-free nonabelian address group, a four-active-role mixed-height target, and a finite complete paid alphabet. This makes the card's broad escape question into an exact three-call construction test.
bottleneck_link: A three-call word would save two of the five direct normalized bit calls (40%) for this target. The exact result finds none; it has no supplier transfer or selected-kappa effect.
stop_rule: Enumerate every ordered pair of the 960 paid factors, join against all 960 right-factor queries, and stop after the full 960^3 three-call domain is covered. Do not enlarge the alphabet after a no-hit result.
evidence: Exact full-formal-algebra join: 921600 ordered two-factor words collapsed to 736361 distinct matrix states; all 960 right queries checked against a separate direct matrix product; zero length-three matches. The direct five-call word passes exact endpoint replay. Parity excludes even lengths and one-call support excludes length one, so the exact minimum for this fixed target and alphabet is five.
